name: gli-gsf-security
description: Security-engineering rules for an interactive gaming platform under the GLI Gaming Security Framework (GLI-GSF-1) — the deep security-controls layer beneath GLI-19's technical-security appendix, owning the infrastructure and network security territory (DNS, firewalls, remote access, hardening, segmentation, IDS/IPS, patching, secure SDLC) and the deep version of access control, data-at-rest, communications and crypto. Covers logical access control (individual credentials, RBAC with least privilege, separation of duties, hashed credential storage, three-attempt lockout, timely deprovisioning, access-attempt and override audit logs with actor), authentication and session authorization (ephemeral per-request authorization never stored on the component, random in-memory session tokens cleared at session end, inactivity timeout, failed-authorization termination), secrets and key management (approved algorithms, key agility with distinct keys per purpose, generation/storage/expiry/rotation lifecycle, trusted-authority certificates), sensitive data at rest (encryption or SoD + access logging, no error-driven auto-clear, durable-write-before-eviction, masking, DLP), network segmentation (production databases isolated from patron-facing servers, logical separation, no single point of DoS, IDS/IPS, 24/7 monitored entry-exit points), communications security (documented secure protocol, encryption + authentication of critical traffic, hardening against malformed messages, always-encrypted public-network traffic), component hardening (remove defaults, one primary function per server, prevent unauthorized server-side programming), DNS security (DNSSEC, MFA-gated changes, restricted zone transfers), remote access and firewalls (default-disabled least-function remote access, application-level firewall at security-domain boundaries, default-deny with no bypass path, anti-spoofing), logging and monitoring (per-component security logs protected against tampering, centralized aggregation, incident detection and escalation, versioned tamper-evident audit-log retention), backup and recovery (at-least-daily immutable backups, off-site redundancy, no lost or duplicated transactions on restart, disaster recovery), change management and secure SDLC (version control, authorized-versions-only, change log, rollback, environments separated from production, release segregation of duties, tested patching), and secure third-party-provider integration (dedicated monitored accounts, encrypted strongly-authenticated segmented communication that cannot route into production). 72 rules mapped to GLI-GSF-1 GIS control ids with GIG1/GIG2/GIG3 assurance tiers
